event.title: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya Minority
event.canonical_title: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya Minority
event.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar is guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority, marking a historic decision as it is the first time a state has been held accountable for genocide by the court. The ruling, passed by a narrow margin of nine votes to six, pertains to the military crackdown in 2017 that resulted in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement of the Rohingya people. The court has called for reparations and the safe return of refugees.

timeline.title: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya Minority
timeline.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar's military committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, marking a historic first for a country being found guilty of genocide. The ruling has been hailed as a significant moment for justice, eliciting emotional responses from the Rohingya community and advocates worldwide. However, Myanmar's government has dismissed the ruling as 'unfair' and a 'great disappointment', raising concerns about its implications for international law and other ongoing genocide allegations, including those against Israel.
key_facts: ICJ ruling finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya.
Ruling is a historic first for a country found guilty of genocide.
Myanmar government calls the ruling 'unfair' and a 'great disappointment'.
The ruling may have implications for other genocide cases, including allegations against Israel.
